meta.headline: Every leap second since 1972 has been added, none ever taken away
meta.seoTitle: Has a leap second ever been taken away?

dek.text: The official record of every leap second since UTC began in 1972 shows each one adding a second to civil time; none has ever subtracted one.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has added a second to civil time; none has ever subtracted one.

description.text: The IERS table of leap seconds runs only one way, from 10 seconds in 1972 to 37 seconds in 2017 — none has ever been subtracted.

assertions.text: The IERS table of TAI-UTC runs from 10 seconds in 1972 to 37 seconds in 2017, rising at every step and never falling.

sections.name: answer
sections.heading: No leap second has ever been taken away

sentences.text: The official leap-second record, kept by the International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service, has only ever moved one way: it opened at 10 seconds in 1972 and stands at 37 seconds as of 2017.

assertions.text: The IERS record of the gap between atomic time and civil time (TAI-UTC) opened at 10 seconds in 1972 and reached 37 seconds in 2017, rising at every step in between.

sentences.text: That settles whether a leap second has ever been subtracted: none has — every adjustment since UTC began has only added a second to civil time.

assertions.text: Every leap second since UTC began in 1972 has added a second to civil time; none has ever subtracted one.
